groups.name: Style rules: wording, spelling and vocabulary
groups.description: Word-level preferences such as British spellings, banned or replaced words, cutting intensifiers, hedges and filler, avoiding contractions, and preferring direct verbs and active voice.
groups.applies_when: Apply to every reply the assistant writes, whatever the topic, because these rules govern all of the user's text.
groups.extras: colour, grey, judgement, okay, email, utilise, whilst, in order to, basically, very, perhaps, contractions, e.g., nominalisations, active voice, double negatives, redundant pairs
examples: User wants redundant pairs like each and every or first and foremost cut from replies.
User wants the word basically removed from every reply, whatever is being explained to them.
User wants the word very-like qualifiers such as quite and rather left out of replies.

groups.name: Style rules: punctuation, formatting and structure
groups.description: Rules on punctuation marks, formatting, number writing, sentence and paragraph structure, and reply length.
groups.applies_when: Apply to every reply the assistant writes, since these rules shape the layout and punctuation of all output.
groups.extras: em dashes, exclamation marks, semicolons, ellipses, ampersands, bold, inline code, parentheses, numbers under ten, percent, paragraph spacing, one idea per sentence, two hundred words, acronyms, rhetorical questions
examples: User wants sentences never started with conjunctions such as and, but or so.
User wants rhetorical questions left out of every reply, whatever the subject being discussed.
User wants each paragraph limited to a single main point, never mixing two separate ideas.

groups.name: Style rules: analogies and metaphors
groups.description: Preferred analogies, metaphors and reference domains the user likes when concepts are explained.
groups.applies_when: Consult whenever an explanation would benefit from an analogy or metaphor, especially for technical, scientific, career or emotional topics.
groups.extras: woodworking, Lego, orchestra, plumbing, recipes, mountain climbing, poker, tides, weather, river delta, ant colony, postal service, bus routes
examples: User likes nature documentary references when discussing animal behavior.
User likes weather metaphors when discussing shifting moods and emotions.
User likes puzzle box analogies when explaining encryption keys simply.

groups.name: Style rules: example themes and programming languages
groups.description: Preferred subject matter for illustrative examples and stories, and which programming languages or platforms to use for code examples by topic.
groups.applies_when: Consult whenever a reply includes examples, sample stories, illustrative scenarios or code snippets.
groups.extras: cats, parrots, foxes, Moorish tilework, haiku, Roman life, rural businesses, low sodium meals, dumbbells, Kotlin, Haskell, Bash, Swift, Dart, Scala, Perl, C sharp, macOS terminal
examples: User enjoys examples featuring picnics beside calm countryside rivers.
User enjoys examples drawn from Viking seafaring life for history.
User prefers workout examples using resistance bands in small apartments.

groups.name: Style rules: units, time frames and sources
groups.description: Conventions for currencies, calendar and scheduling units, and which kinds of sources to favour when citing information.
groups.applies_when: Consult when a reply involves money estimates, dates or timelines, or cites sources and evidence.
groups.extras: Thai baht, Brazilian reais, rupees, week numbers, fiscal quarters, school terms, lunar calendar, peer reviewed journals, museum guides, oral history, government health guidance
examples: User prefers prices in Indian rupees for trips around Kerala.
User tends to favour government health agency guidance for nutrition topics.
User prefers fiscal quarters when discussing business planning timelines.

groups.name: Task procedures: data logging, lookups and spreadsheets
groups.description: Workflows where the user wants records tracked as spreadsheet rows or data pulled from databases, CRM or support tickets.
groups.applies_when: Consult before doing any tracking, tallying, budgeting, data lookup or record-keeping task with tools.
groups.extras: spreadsheet_append, sql_query, crm_lookup, support_ticket_search, drive_search, web_search
examples: When checking how often a product error message appears, User wants occurrences counted with sql_query and matching tickets reviewed using support_ticket_search.
For tracking office supply reorders, User wants each order request appended as a row with spreadsheet_append and the office manager notified through slack_post.
For planning a team hackathon prize budget, User wants past prize costs found with drive_search and the new amounts logged via spreadsheet_append.

groups.name: Task procedures: documents and team communication
groups.description: Workflows for drafting documents, newsletters, case studies and updates and sharing them through email, Slack or Notion.
groups.applies_when: Consult before drafting, publishing or sending written work or announcements to colleagues or partners with tools.
groups.extras: docs_create, email_send, slack_post, notion_search, notion_create_page, github_search_code, web_search, support_ticket_search
examples: For running an A/B test readout, User wants the raw results pulled with sql_query and the writeup drafted in a new docs_create document.
For planning a team trivia night, User wants question ideas gathered with web_search and the final quiz written up in a new docs_create document.
When compiling a monthly newsletter for the department, User wants highlights gathered with notion_search and the finished newsletter sent out through email_send.

groups.name: Task procedures: tickets, calendar and file storage
groups.description: Workflows for filing issues, scheduling events or reminders, and uploading or archiving files.
groups.applies_when: Consult before creating tickets, scheduling meetings or reminders, or storing and sharing files with tools.
